ADJ.name: adjective
ADJ.definition: A word that typically modifies a noun and describes a property of its referent, such as size, colour, age or quality. Adjectives can also be predicates ("The car is red").

ADP.name: adposition
ADP.definition: A preposition or postposition: a word that combines with a noun phrase and marks its relation to the rest of the clause (English "in", "of", "by").

ADV.name: adverb
ADV.definition: A word that typically modifies a verb, an adjective or another adverb, expressing time, place, manner, degree and similar notions ("quickly", "very", "here").

AUX.name: auxiliary
AUX.definition: A function word that accompanies a lexical verb to express tense, aspect, mood, voice or polarity ("is eating", "has eaten", "will go", "can swim"). In UD, copulas are also AUX.

CCONJ.name: coordinating conjunction
CCONJ.definition: A word that links two units of equal syntactic status without making one depend on the other ("and", "or", "but").

DET.name: determiner
DET.definition: A word that modifies a noun phrase and expresses its reference or quantity rather than a descriptive property: articles, demonstratives and many quantifiers ("the", "this", "every").

INTJ.name: interjection
INTJ.definition: A word used as an exclamation or reaction, typically outside the syntax of the clause ("oh", "wow", "yes").

NOUN.name: noun
NOUN.definition: A word that typically denotes a person, place, thing, animal or idea and can head a noun phrase ("child", "rice", "idea").

NUM.name: numeral
NUM.definition: A word expressing a number, written in letters or digits ("three", "3", "2026").

PART.name: particle
PART.definition: A function word that does not fit the other classes and marks a grammatical notion such as negation or possession. In English, "not"/"n't", infinitival "to" and possessive "'s" are PART.

PRON.name: pronoun
PRON.definition: A word that substitutes for a noun phrase and whose reference depends on context ("she", "it", "who", "themselves").

PROPN.name: proper noun
PROPN.definition: A noun that is the name of a specific individual, place or organization ("Mary", "Manila", "Google").

PUNCT.name: punctuation
PUNCT.definition: A non-alphabetic character that delimits linguistic units in written text.

SCONJ.name: subordinating conjunction
SCONJ.definition: A conjunction that introduces a subordinate clause and marks it as dependent on another clause ("because", "if", "that" introducing a complement clause).

SYM.name: symbol
SYM.definition: A word-like unit written with symbols rather than letters, such as "$", "%", "+" or an emoji, used like a word rather than as punctuation.

VERB.name: verb
VERB.definition: A word that typically denotes an event or state and can head a clause, taking arguments such as a subject and an object ("eat", "know", "arrive").

X.name: other
X.definition: A word that cannot be assigned a real part-of-speech category, such as a foreign-language fragment or a word that is cut off.
